SECTION I Informational Matters COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: BUS 101X | Business: Explore and Innovate New Temporary Course (1 cr.) Introductory seminar for incoming College of Business students.
Introduces practical skills needed to succeed in the College of Business and in careers; illustrates the importance of business innovation, entrepreneurial thinking, connections, and team skills; and explores majors, minors, and potential career paths in fields of interest.
Required of all first-year business students and transfer business students with fewer than 30 credits. (Seminar/Online) Pre: For Business majors only.

Not open to students who completed URI101 for credit.

SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: ART 231 | Print Media I Change description Create online version of existing course (3 crs.) COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: LDR 190 | Introduction to Leadership Issues Change college (CHS to BUS) & course code (HDF to LDR) Create online version of existing course (3 crs.) Leadership development course focusing on leadership theories, personal and academic adjustment issues, civic leadership and community service and basic communication skills.
Core requirement for the minor in leadership studies (Lec. 3) Pre: permission of instructor.

COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: EDC 455 | Language Arts Methods in Elementary & Middle School Teaching Change prerequisites Create online version of existing course (2 crs.) Language arts and reading principles and practices of guiding children in the skillful use of basic means of communication (speaking, listening, writing, and reading) in the elementary and middle school classroom. (Lec. 2) Pre: EDC 424, 456, 457, 458, 459, acceptance into the elementary education program, and concurrent enrollment in EDC 402 and 460.
Not for graduate credit.
EDC 460 | Supervised Methods Practicum II Change prerequisites & corequisites Create online version of existing course (2 crs.) Supervised field experience related to evaluation of elementary students and methods courses: teaching special needs students, social studies, and language arts.
Students will observe and teach.
Students meet periodically throughout the semester to focus on issues of classroom management. (Practicum) Pre: EDC 424, 456, 457, 458, 459, acceptance into the elementary education program, taken or concurrent enrollment in EDC 402, and concurrent enrollment in EDC 455.
Not for graduate credit.

COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: CVE 453 | Analysis of Indeterminate Structures Change title and description Create online version of existing course (3 crs.) Analysis of indeterminate structural systems (trusses, beams, and frames) using classical and matrix methods based on both flexibility and stiffness approaches.
Serves as an introduction to finite element methods. (Lec. 3) Pre: CVE 354 or equivalent.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: EEC 450 | Experimental Economics Change description & prerequisites Create online version of existing course (3 crs.) Cross-listed (EEC), ECN, MKT 450.
This course provides an introduction to the methods and practice of experimental economics and behavioral economics with a focus on the environment.
Students will learn the fundamentals of behavioral and experimental economics and important findings from experiments. (Lec. 3) Pre: EEC 105 or ECN 201 or permission of instructor.

COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: CMD 274 | Communication Processes Temporary course to permanent Create online version of existing course (2 crs.) This course focuses on the structural properties of language as a system of communication. (Online) Pre: sophomore standing.
HDF 342 | Working with Families in Early Childhood Change prerequisites Create online version of existing course (2 crs.) This course focuses on the structural properties of language as a system of communication. (Online) Pre: sophomore standing.
HDF 472 | Traumatic Stress in Families Temporary course to permanent Create online version of existing course (2 crs.) This course focuses on the structural properties of language as a system of communication. (Online) Pre: sophomore standing.
NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: SCM 202 | Introduction to Remote Sports Production Create online version of existing course (4 crs.) This course introduces students to live athletics event production for television broadcast.
The course covers crew positions, equipment, and techniques commonly employed.
Students will also participate in actual live campus broadcasts.

COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: CVE 353 | Civil Engineering Materials Create online version of existing course (3 crs.) Processing, microstructure, properties, and applications of civil engineering materials, focusing on portland cement concrete, steel, asphalt concrete, wood, and composites. (Lec. 3) Pre: CVE 220.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: HDF 496 | Applied Research in Human Development & Family Science (1-3 crs.) Literature, laboratory work, and/or individual research under the direction of a departmental family member. (Independent Study) Pre: Sophomore standing and permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
HLT 201 | Public Health Topics in the 21st Century Create online version of existing course (3 crs.) This course is designed to introduce students to current and controversial public health topics.
Students will be required to explore the implications of numerous current topics from a public health perspective. (Lec. 3) Pre: HLT 101G, for Health Studies majors only.

Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-2
November 14, 2024 Faculty Senate Meeting
Context (from JCODL 2022-2023 final report): “Several years ago (circa 2013), URI adopted definitions of online and blended learning (Face to face [< 25% online], Blended [25-75% online], and Online [75-100% online]), with the implicit, but unstated, assumption that the online portion was asynchronous. The COVID era of remote instruction gave rise to additional approaches to remote instruction and the need to reflect all available modality options and to provide clear, comprehensible and accessible definitions and descriptions for the benefit of faculty and students.”
Existing Language:
https://web.uri.edu/registration-records/faculty-staff-advisors/class-scheduling-process/.
“In-person (I): A course with no more than 24.9% of instruction delivered online. All courses are assumed to be in-person unless otherwise approved by Faculty Senate.
Blended (B): A course delivered 25%-74.9% online.
Online (O): A course delivered at least 75% online. Course must be approved as online by Faculty Senate to be scheduled as such.”
Proposed Language:

(To be inserted into Chapter 8 of the University Manual, “Academic Regulations.”)
“8.30.30 Course Modality
In-person: All instruction occurs in a specified physical location and on specified days/times.
In-person and online asynchronous: Instruction combines both in-person meetings on specified days/times and online asynchronous instruction. The schedule of instruction and the weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction are clear to students in the syllabus on the first day of class.
Online synchronous: All instruction occurs online at specified days/times.
Online synchronous and asynchronous: All instruction occurs online in a combination of synchronous meetings on specified days/times and asynchronous instruction. The schedule of instruction and the weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction are clear to students in the syllabus.
Online asynchronous: All instruction occurs online with no synchronous meetings required at specified days/times (outside of optional online office hours/meetings). The weekly time commitment to online asynchronous instruction is clear to students in the syllabus.”

FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION
NOVEMBER 14, 2024
Joint Curriculum & Standards Committee and Faculty Senate Executive Committee Report #2024-2025-01
The following matter was discussed and recommended by the Curriculum & Standards Committee at their October 31, 2024 meeting, and later supported by the Faculty Senate Executive Committee. It is now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Context: Currently, courses approved for online formats during the traditional academic calendar (Fall/Spring 14-weeks, J-Term, and Summer 5- and 10-weeks) must complete a full curricular review to be added to the URI Online Accelerated calendar (7-week Fall, Spring, and Summer sessions).
Proposed: Any course approved for online instruction is thereby approved for being offered in all online semester calendars: 14-week, J-Term, Summer (5 and 10 week), and accelerated 7-week terms.
